# Methods

## Data

This retrospective observational study used all EuroLeague games from 2016–17 to 2024–25 (`{python} A["seasons"]` seasons, `{python} n(A["games"])` games) from the public EuroLeague application programming interface: box scores, play-by-play logs, shot coordinates and the player registry. Five-on-five lineup segments were reconstructed from substitution events, with starting lineups taken from the box score; segments with at least one estimated possession (`{python} n(L["segment_N"])`) were used. Segment net rating was the home-minus-away point difference per 100 possessions, with possessions estimated as field-goal attempts + 0.44 × free-throw attempts − offensive rebounds + turnovers [@kubatko2007starting]. Only public performance data were used, so ethical approval was not required. Reporting follows the STROBE statement where applicable.

## Player value measures

PIR was taken from the official box score (points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and fouls drawn, minus missed field goals, missed free throws, turnovers, shots blocked and fouls committed) and expressed per 40 minutes (PIR40). VAL40 is a closely related composite used in the author's doctoral thesis on these data, which omits fouls and blocked shots. Box-score values were computed only for players with at least 60 minutes in the relevant period, to avoid extreme per-40-minute rates. RAPM was estimated by ridge regression of segment net rating on indicators for the ten players on court (+1 home, −1 away), weighted by possessions, with a home-advantage intercept; players with fewer than 300 possessions shared one replacement-level coefficient, and the penalty was chosen by five-fold cross-validation with games as groups [@grassetti2020extended].

## Role bias

Players were assigned to one of five functional roles (ball handler, wing, stretch forward, interior big, rim protector) derived in a companion analysis by Gaussian-mixture clustering of possession shares, shot profile and assist-network variables, with the number of roles chosen by player-level bootstrap stability [@hennig2007cluster]. Because several role variables (rebound, block, steal, assist, turnover and foul rates) are also components of PIR, role differences in PIR are partly expected by construction. Role dependence was therefore assessed in three ways: (1) unconditionally; (2) conditionally on RAPM, as the partial η² of role in a regression of PIR40 on RAPM and role, which asks whether players with the same on-court impact receive different PIR values depending on their role; and (3) with an alternative five-role partition derived only from variables that are not PIR components (shot profile, assist network, usage and three-point attempt rate). Each player's main role was the role in which he played most minutes. For players with at least `{python} V["asgari_dakika"]` career minutes (n = `{python} V["oyuncu_N"]`), role bias was quantified as η², the share of between-player variance in each value measure explained by role, with 95% confidence intervals from `{python} n(V["B"])` player bootstrap resamples. Because ridge shrinkage could compress differences between roles, RAPM was also estimated with a weaker penalty (λ = 1,000). Because a noisier measure has a lower η² for a given true role effect, split-half reliability was estimated by computing each measure separately from even- and odd-numbered games (players with at least half the minimum minutes in each half), corrected with the Spearman–Brown formula, and η² was divided by this reliability.

## Out-of-time predictive validity

Value measures were computed from 2016–2022 data and used to predict 2023–2024 segment net ratings: the home-minus-away sum of PIR40 or VAL40 entered a weighted linear regression, and RAPM predicted directly. Players not seen in the training period were given the league average under all measures; players seen with fewer than 300 possessions received RAPM's replacement-level coefficient. Possession-weighted R² was computed for each predictor, and differences between predictors were given 95% confidence intervals from 500 bootstrap resamples of test games.

## Within-season validity of lineup value

Each season was split at its median game. Player values were computed from information available at the split only: PIR40 and VAL40 from the first half and, to match the data available to RAPM, from all earlier data; RAPM from all earlier segments; and first-half minutes as a measure of the coach's own ranking. For every second-half segment, the summed value of the five players was standardised within team-season, and segment net rating was regressed on it, adjusting for the summed RAPM of the opposing five and for home advantage. Slopes were given 95% confidence intervals from `{python} n(I["B"])` bootstrap resamples of team-seasons (n = `{python} I["takim_sezon_N"]`). Because box-score values were undefined for some players, slopes were also estimated on the common subset of segments in which all pooled measures and minutes were defined, and differences between RAPM and each other measure were estimated in the same bootstrap resamples. Each segment entered the analysis once for each team.

## Lineup optimisation

For each team-season, integer linear programming selected the five players (from those with at least 100 first-half minutes) with the highest total value, without role constraints, with at least one rim protector (the constraint used in earlier work), or with a balanced composition (at least one ball handler and one or two interior players). The coach benchmark was the five players with most first-half minutes, selected under the same constraint (that is, the same integer programme maximising minutes instead of value). Second-half segments containing at least four of the selected players were compared with the team's other second-half segments using net rating adjusted for opponent RAPM and home advantage; differences, and paired differences between each optimised five and the coach benchmark under the same constraint, were given team-season bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. We report the share of second-half possessions in which each selected five was observed and the mean number of players it shared with the coach benchmark.
